samples.summary: Empty-color normalization only recognizes the bare `''`, not the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` / whitespace spellings the codebase elsewhere defines as "empty"
samples.evidence: `clearEmptyStringKeys` tests `(style[key] as unknown) === ''` (types.ts:277). But `color`/`backgroundColor` are typed `StoredColor` (types.ts:178-180), and `isEmptyStoredColor` in model/color.ts:67-74 deliberately treats BOTH `''`/whitespace strings AND `{ kind:'srgb', value:'' }` as "no color" — the doc comment there says the wrapped form is produced by "a theme-color migration or PPTX import". A write path that hands `applyInlineStyle` such a wrapped-empty color (e.g. the format painter, text-editor.ts:2903 `applyStyleToSelection(range, resolved)`, copying a style read off a PPTX-imported run) reproduces exactly the #793 defect this change fixes: `storedColorsEqual({kind:'srgb',value:''}, undefined)` is false (color.ts:157-160), so the run can never re-merge in `normalizeInlines`, and the dead value is written to the CRDT. The paint side normalizes it away, so the symptom is the permanent run split / "a highlight is present" reads, not a visual one.
searchedFor: grep for other normalize* helpers on style write paths

samples.summary: Inline path leaves the cleared key present-holding-`undefined` in the in-memory/cached style, the exact store-divergence the cell path was changed to avoid
samples.evidence: `applyInlineStyle` merges with `{ ...inline.style, ...resolvedStyle }` (block-helpers.ts:348), so after a clear the run's style object still has the key with value `undefined` whenever the run is not re-merged with a neighbour (e.g. styling the whole block: applyStyle(block, 0, len, { backgroundColor: '' }) yields one inline whose style has `'backgroundColor' in style === true`). The Yorkie tree, in contrast, removes the attribute (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1927), so a reload/fresh store gives `false`. This is precisely the inconsistency the diff calls out and fixes for cells (memory.ts:284-293 deletes the key, with the comment "'backgroundColor' in cell.style would answer true here and false there"), but the same deletion was not applied on the inline path. The diff's own inline tests avoid the case by styling a sub-range so re-merge drops the key.
searchedFor: read applyInlineStyle and normalizeInlines in packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts
grep for `' in style'` / Object.keys(style) presence checks in packages/{docs,frontend,slides}/src

samples.summary: Newly guarded `styleByPath` can make `applyCellStyle` emit zero Yorkie ops, so a no-op cell-style call produces no change event for subscribers/undo
samples.evidence: `if (Object.keys(attrs).length > 0) tree.styleByPath(cellPath, attrs)` (line 2488) combined with `removeNodeStyle` returning early when `attrsToRemove.length === 0` (line 284) means an `applyCellStyle` call whose merged style serializes to nothing and clears nothing (e.g. `applyCellStyle(id, r, c, {})`, or a clear of a key that was never set on an otherwise unstyled cell) runs `doc.update` with no operation at all. Previously `styleByPath(cellPath, {})` always ran. No data is lost — `attrs` is derived from the full merged style, so it is empty only when there is nothing to write — but any subscriber/undo entry that relied on the update producing a change is now skipped. Worth confirming the editor's snapshot/history does not end up with an empty undo step.
searchedFor: grep applyCellStyle call sites in packages/{docs,frontend,slides}/src
